text:
ashley-cs: FYI — customer reported a surge of 401s after we revoked an API key and applied new k8s secrets via Helm. They updated the secret, rollout finished, but sidecar proxies still present old token to upstream.

mike-infra: Which sidecar? envoy sidecar or our internal auth-proxy?

ashley-cs: auth-proxy sidecar (service runs app + auth-proxy as a sidecar). Cluster: eu-prod-1. Customer did a Helm upgrade to update k8s secret named `company-api-key`.

john-eng: Typical culprit: sidecar reads secret into env on container start and keeps it, while secret was mounted as file for another process. Need to confirm how auth-proxy loads creds (env vs file vs sidecar cache).

sara-support: Customer logs attached: 
- Upstream response: 401 from token verifier
- Sidecar log shows `using cached token from in-memory cache` at startup

mike-infra: Can the customer run `kubectl rollout restart deploy/<svc>`? If sidecar env var was injected at pod start, rolling restart should pick new value.

ashley-cs: They already tried a Helm rollout (helm upgrade --install) which replaced k8s Secret, but pods were not restarted due to unchanged pod template checksum (secret not referenced as envFrom). They only patched secret, not forced pod restart.

john-eng: Oof. If the sidecar caches the token in-memory and we didn't restart the container, it will keep using old creds until restart or until the sidecar refresh path is triggered. Does auth-proxy support TTL-based refresh from Vault?

sara-support: Customer says they expected automatic secret propagation via sidecar injector. Injector mutated pod to mount secret as file at /etc/secrets/apikey but auth-proxy was reading from ENV var `API_KEY` populated by legacy init container. So mismatch.

mike-infra: Steps to reproduce (for our infra team):
```
# simulate secret update
kubectl create secret generic test-apikey --from-literal=key=oldtoken -n test
# start pod that sets env from secret (init container writes env file)
# upgrade secret
kubectl create secret generic test-apikey --from-literal=key=newtoken -n test -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f -
# note: pods won't restart automatically if podTemplateSpec unchanged
```

john-eng: Quick mitigation for customer: force restart pods in namespace/app (kubectl rollout restart deploy/<name>) or delete pod one by one. That will ensure containers read new env or mounted file.

ashley-cs: Customer tried `kubectl delete pod` but since their deployment uses podDisruptionBudget and high availability, they were trying to avoid full restart during peak. They want a non-disruptive approach.

mike-infra: Non-disruptive options: if auth-proxy supports reading from a mounted file and watching for changes, we can recommend switching to file mount + inotify-based reload (requires sidecar change). Otherwise, add a short-lived sidecar that periodically reloads secrets into the running process via API. Both are product changes.

john-eng: Short-term workaround: patch deployment to include `checksum/secret: <hash>` annotation so Helm/KS will trigger pod template change on secret update. Example: annotate with the secret resourceVersion or hash of its data. That makes upgrades non-ambiguous and safer.

sara-support: Sent customer a step-by-step safe patch:
```
# compute hash locally (example)
HASH=$(kubectl get secret company-api-key -n prod -o json | sha1sum | awk '{print $1}')
kubectl patch deploy my-service -n prod -p "{\"spec\":{\"template\":{\"metadata\":{\"annotations\":{\"secret-checksum/company-api-key\":\"$HASH\"}}}}}"
```

ashley-cs: Customer executed patch -> pods restarted one-by-one, new tokens presented, 401s cleared. They still want root cause analysis and guidance so this doesn't recur.

mike-infra: Root cause summary we should send them: 1) Secret was updated in k8s but pod template did not change -> containers not restarted. 2) Auth-proxy reads token at process start (env or init-file) and caches in-memory, no hot-reload. 3) Sidecar injector mounted file but app used env from init container -> config mismatch. 4) Result: old token continued to be used until container restart.

john-eng: Action items:
- Docs: add a KB on "secret rotation steps for sidecar-based auth" explaining env vs mount differences and recommended annotations.
- QOE (engineering): add optional hot-reload to auth-proxy (watch mounted file or provide admin reload endpoint).
- DevEx: provide Helm helper to auto-annotate deployments with secret checksum.

sara-support: Customer accepted mitigation and requested a case note. I documented timeline + commands and linked to the patch we recommended.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for my-service completed (duration 00:03:12) :white_check_mark:

ashley-cs: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all — will file the KB ticket in docs and tag eng for the hot-reload feature request. :thumbsup:
